proposals.before: His great-grandmother, Lady Li of Longxi, was posthumously titled Empress Mingzhen.
proposals.after: His great-great-grandmother, Lady Li of Longxi, was posthumously titled Empress Mingzhen.
proposals.reason: 高祖母 is the wife of the fourth-generation ancestor (四代祖), i.e. a great-great-grandmother; 曾祖母 in s0010 is the great-grandmother.

proposals.before: The Gaozu's great-grandmother was Lady Li of Longxi, posthumously honored as Empress Mingzhen.
proposals.after: Gaozu's great-great-grandmother was Lady Li of Longxi, posthumously honored as Empress Mingzhen.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats the generation error and the awkward 'The Gaozu's'; 高祖母 is great-great-grandmother.

proposals.before: After Mingzong acceded, Jin Gaozu was stationed at the Northern Capital as military governor; remembering the emperor's earlier rescue, he had him transferred to his own command and appointed him commander of the gate guards.
proposals.after: After Mingzong acceded, Jin Gaozu was stay-behind prefect of the Northern Capital; remembering the emperor's earlier rescue, he had him transferred to his own command and appointed him commander of the gate guards.
proposals.reason: 北京留守 is the stay-behind/regent of the Northern Capital, not a military governor (節度使).

proposals.before: The Khitan ruler escorted Jin Gaozu to Shangdang. Pointing at the future emperor, he told Gaozu, "This commander is very caola—without grave cause do not cast him aside."
proposals.after: The Khitan ruler escorted Jin Gaozu to Shangdang. Pointing at the future emperor, he told Gaozu, "This commander is very fierce and capable—without grave cause do not cast him aside."
proposals.reason: 操剌 is left untranslated as 'caola', which is not English and obscures the Khitan ruler's praise.

proposals.before: In the third month of the fifth year he was made military governor of the Ye capital and retained command of the palace guard horse and foot.
proposals.after: In the third month of the fifth year he was made stay-behind governor of the Ye capital and concurrently commander-in-chief of the palace guard horse and foot.
proposals.reason: 鄴都留守 is a capital stay-behind post, not a military governorship (節度使).

proposals.before: In the third month of the fifth year he was transferred to military governor of the Ye capital while also serving as Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard's cavalry and infantry.
proposals.after: In the third month of the fifth year he was transferred to stay-behind governor of the Ye capital while also serving as Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard's cavalry and infantry.
proposals.reason: 鄴都留守 is mistranslated as military governor.

proposals.before: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was made military governor of the Northern Capital and commissioner of the Hedong circuit.
proposals.after: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was made stay-behind governor of the Northern Capital and military commissioner of Hedong.
proposals.reason: 北京留守 is a stay-behind governorship; only 河東節度使 is a military commissionership.

proposals.before: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was appointed military governor of the Northern Capital and military commissioner of Hedong.
proposals.after: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was appointed stay-behind governor of the Northern Capital and military commissioner of Hedong.
proposals.reason: 北京留守 is not a military governor post.

proposals.before: In the first month of 944 the Khitan invaded the south; their ruler marched a great host to Chunzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei through Yanmen Pass.
proposals.after: In the first month of 944 the Khitan invaded the south; their ruler marched a great host to Chanzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei through Yanmen Pass.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.

proposals.before: In the first month of the first year of Kaiyun, the Khitan marched south; the Khitan ruler led a great army straight to Chunzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei to lead troops into Yanmen.
proposals.after: In the first month of the first year of Kaiyun, the Khitan marched south; the Khitan ruler led a great army straight to Chanzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei to lead troops into Yanmen.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.

proposals.before: On gengwu Zhao Hui of the Fengguo command at Shaan, Hou Zhang, and Wang Yan killed the Khitan supervisor Liu Yuan and his deputy; Hui declared himself acting military governor.
proposals.after: On gengwu Zhao Hui of the Fengguo command at Shaan, Hou Zhang, and Wang Yan killed the Khitan supervisor and vice commissioner Liu Yuan; Hui declared himself acting military governor.
proposals.reason: Chinese 殺契丹監軍及副使劉願 names Liu Yuan with both titles, not a second unnamed deputy.

proposals.before: The Khitan then appointed Hui military governor of Shaan, Hou Zhang commander of local horse and foot, and Wang Yan his deputy, but they refused the orders.
proposals.after: The Khitan then appointed Hui acting military governor of Shaanzhou's forces, Hou Zhang commander of the prefecture's cavalry and infantry, and Wang Yan vice commander, but they refused the orders.
proposals.reason: Chinese 陜州兵馬留後 is an acting command of forces, not a full military governorship of Shaan.

proposals.before: The troops made Hui commander, Zhang vice commander and patrol commissioner, and sent Hanlun to Jinyang with a memorial of submission.))〉
proposals.after: The troops made Hui commander, Zhang vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief disciplinary officer, and sent his son Hanlun to Jinyang with a memorial of submission.))〉
proposals.reason: 都虞候 is a military disciplinary office, not a registrar, and 其子 should be retained as his son.

proposals.before: The crowd asked Hui to be commander, Zhang to be vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief registrar, and then sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.))〉
proposals.after: The crowd asked Hui to be commander, Zhang to be vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief disciplinary officer, and then sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.))〉
proposals.reason: 都虞候 is not a registrar.

proposals.before: On guiwei the bandit Wang Qiong of Chunzhou cut the pontoon bridge with his followers; Qiong was defeated and killed.
proposals.after: On guiwei the bandit Wang Qiong of Chanzhou cut the pontoon bridge with his followers; Qiong was defeated and killed.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.

proposals.before: On the day guiwei the bandit chief Wang Qiong of Chunzhou and his followers cut the prefecture's pontoon bridge; Qiong was defeated and died.
proposals.after: On the day guiwei the bandit chief Wang Qiong of Chanzhou and his followers cut the prefecture's pontoon bridge; Qiong was defeated and died.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.

proposals.before: The Khitan had appointed their kinsman Lang'e military governor of Chunzhou; greedy and brutal, he made life miserable for officials and commoners alike.
proposals.after: The Khitan had appointed their kinsman Lang'e military governor of Chanzhou; greedy and brutal, he made life miserable for officials and commoners alike.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.

proposals.before: At that time the Khitan appointed their clansman Lang'e military governor of Chunzhou; Lang'e was greedy and cruel by nature, and officials and people suffered under him.
proposals.after: At that time the Khitan appointed their clansman Lang'e military governor of Chanzhou; Lang'e was greedy and cruel by nature, and officials and people suffered under him.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.

proposals.before: On New Year's Day of the third month an edict remitted all miscellaneous levies in Hedong beyond the established taxes.
proposals.after: On the first day of the third month an edict remitted all miscellaneous levies in Hedong beyond the established taxes.
proposals.reason: 丙戌朔 marks the first day of the third month, not the New Year; the idiomatic English invents a New Year date.

proposals.before: On the day gengxu the Emperor appointed Liu Chong, Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Capital's cavalry and infantry and Defender of Sizhou and Acting Grand Guardian, Grand Guardian of Taiyuan and Acting Grand Marshal; Guo Congyi, chief registrar of the Northern Capital's horse and foot, Defender of Zhengzhou and Acting Grand Guardian; Li Hongxin, commander of the left wing of the Northern Capital's Xingjie army, Prefect of Chenzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Shang Hongqian, commander of the right wing of the Xingjie army, Prefect of Shanzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Gai Wan, commander of the left wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Caizhou; Zhou Hui, commander of the right wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Puzhou; and Zhu Fengqian, commander of the Baoning army, Prefect of Suizhou.
proposals.after: On the day gengxu the Emperor appointed Liu Chong, Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Capital's cavalry and infantry, Defender of Sizhou and Acting Grand Guardian, Yin of Taiyuan and Acting Grand Marshal; Guo Congyi, chief registrar of the Northern Capital's horse and foot, Defender of Zhengzhou and Acting Grand Guardian; Li Hongxin, commander of the left wing of the Northern Capital's Xingjie army, Prefect of Chenzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Shang Hongqian, commander of the right wing of the Xingjie army, Prefect of Shanzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Gai Wan, commander of the left wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Caizhou; Zhou Hui, commander of the right wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Puzhou; and Zhu Fengqian, commander of the Baoning army, Prefect of Suizhou.
proposals.reason: 太原尹 is the Yin of Taiyuan, not Grand Guardian.

proposals.before: Shi Hongzhao was made military governor of Xuzhou and commander of the palace guard infantry with the rank of Acting Grand Tutor;
proposals.after: Shi Hongzhao was made military governor of Xu Prefecture and commander of the palace guard infantry with the rank of Acting Grand Tutor;
proposals.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture, not 徐州 Xuzhou.

proposals.before: On jiazi the eldest son Chengxun was made general-in-chief of the Left Guard, Chengyou great general of the Left Guard, and Chengxun the third son great general of the Right Guard; Lady Song of Pengcheng was created Princess Yongning, and the nephew Chengyun was made general-in-chief of the Right Guard.
proposals.after: On jiazi the eldest son Chengxun was made general-in-chief of the Left Guard, the second son Chengyou great general of the Left Guard, and the third son Chengxun great general of the Right Guard; Lady Song of Pengcheng was created Princess Yongning, and the nephew Chengyun was made general-in-chief of the Right Guard.
proposals.reason: The third son is 承勛, not a second Chengxun repeating 承訓.

proposals.before: When Mouhan arrived he killed the former Chunzhou governor Pan Huan in Luoyang.
proposals.after: When Mouhan arrived he killed the former Chanzhou governor Pan Huan in Luoyang.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou; the English romanization corrupts the prefecture name.

proposals.before: When Mouhan arrived he killed Pan Huan, former military governor of Chunzhou, at Luoyang.
proposals.after: When Mouhan arrived he killed Pan Huan, former military governor of Chanzhou, at Luoyang.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou; Chunzhou is a wrong romanization of the same office.

proposals.before: On jiaxu Wang Shouen was made Acting Grand Marshal and the former Dizhou prefect Murong Yanchao was made military governor of Chunzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.
proposals.after: On jiaxu Wang Shouen was made Acting Grand Marshal and the former Dizhou prefect Murong Yanchao was made military governor of Chanzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 澶州 should be Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.

proposals.before: On the day jiaxu Wang Shouen, military governor of Luzhou, was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal, and Murong Yanchao, former Prefect of Dizhou, was made military governor of Chunzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.
proposals.after: On the day jiaxu Wang Shouen, military governor of Luzhou, was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal, and Murong Yanchao, former Prefect of Dizhou, was made military governor of Chanzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 澶州 should be Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.

decisions.reason: 高祖母 follows 四代祖湍 and precedes 曾祖昂, so she is the fourth-generation ancestress (great-great-grandmother), not the great-grandmother.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高祖母隴西李氏

decisions.after: His great-great-grandmother was Lady Li of Longxi, posthumously honored as Empress Mingzhen.
decisions.reason: 高祖母 is the kinship term great-great-grandmother, not “Gaozu’s” mother or grandmother; the generation must be corrected without treating 高祖 as a personal title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高祖母隴西李氏，追謚明貞皇后。

decisions.after: After Mingzong acceded, Jin Gaozu was stay-behind governor of the Northern Capital; remembering the emperor's earlier rescue, he had him transferred to his own command and appointed him commander of the gate guards.
decisions.reason: 北京留守 is a capital stay-behind post, not a military governorship; “prefect” is also wrong, since 留守 is not 刺史.
